name: 11-coevolving-growing-network
title: Dynamics on a growing network — reactors entrain as the graph is built
question: Can SBML reactor dynamics run on a network whose topology is itself being built by a process-bigraph reaction, and do newcomers entrain?
hypothesis: Running the Family-B reactors + transport on a graph that a Family-A growth reaction is simultaneously building, each newcomer joins at its own phase and is pulled into synchrony by the dense local coupling — the full synthesis of dynamics OF and ON the network.
objective: Run the growing_repressilator_network composite — SBML reactors + transport on a topology that a PBG reaction reconfigures during the run — and measure synchrony.
description:
Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction; each newcomer entrains, and the growing network synchronises.

This is a Family-C (co-evolution) study: a Family-A reaction reconfigures the graph WHILE the Family-B SBML reactors + inter-node transport run on it. See viz/ for the concentration-on-network animation and the per-node time series.
claim: Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction: the system stays bounded and oscillating, and most newcomers entrain through the dense local coupling — but synchronisability is topology-dependent, with weakly-attached (low-degree) nodes lagging the synchronised core.

findings.name: growing_repressilator_network-result
findings.summary: Continuous SBML dynamics run correctly on a network being built node-by-node by a PBG reaction: the system stays bounded and oscillating, and most newcomers entrain through the dense local coupling — but synchronisability is topology-dependent, with weakly-attached (low-degree) nodes lagging the synchronised core.
findings.detail: The headline synthesis: a forest-fire growth reaction builds the network node-by-node WHILE a COPASI/SBML Repressilator runs in every node and proteins diffuse along the (changing) edges. Each newcomer arrives at its own limit-cycle phase; the dense local coupling pulls most of them into the synchronised core, so the across-node spread stays small relative to the oscillation amplitude even as the network grows. Synchronisability is topology-dependent, though: a newcomer that attaches with only a single edge couples weakly and lags (Rodrigues et al. 2016). This is the companion to the uniform-degree rewiring study (12), which synchronises fully. Topology (dynamics OF the network) and continuous multi-species node state (dynamics ON the network) co-evolve in one process-bigraph composite.

followup_proposals.title: Model-agnostic node reactor (Brusselator)
followup_proposals.motivation: Families B/C hardcode the Repressilator; the architecture should accept any SBML model with no code change.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Point NetworkSBMLReactors at a Brusselator SBML instead; the reactor + transport code is model-independent, so reaction–diffusion patterning should emerge on the network.

followup_proposals.title: Degree-resolved entrainment analysis
followup_proposals.motivation: This study found low-degree newcomers lag the synchronised core; the dependence on node degree should be quantified.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Measure a per-node phase-lock order parameter as a function of node degree over the growth trajectory.
